newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia wheels out new weapon in anti-drug war.
newsitem.headline: Colombia wheels out new weapon in anti-drug war.

text.p: Colombia has unveiled a new weapon in its fight against illicit drug crops, an all-weather herbicide called Imazapyr that should boost the most ambitious eradication programme in Latin America, authorities said on Monday.
Sources at the anti-narcotics division of the National Police said the first 150 acres (60 hectares) of coca leaf were sprayed with the herbicide over the weekend in southeastern Guaviare province.
The chemical can be used even in wet and windy conditions unlike glyphosate, a spray which has been used for fumigation with mixed results until now.

Colombia's U.S.-backed drug crop eradication programme is the most ambitious in Latin America, according to Western drug experts. This year the government has agreed to destroy 44,500 acres (18,000 hectares) of coca leaf, the raw material for cocaine, and 9,885 acres (4,000 hectares) of opium poppy.
But heavy rains and high winds in the south and east of the country early in the year meant that fumigation, using the glyphosate spray, was hampered.

There were initial fears that eradication targets may not be achieved but in a recent interview, Col. Leonardo Gallego, head of the police's anti-narcotics division, said he was confident the agreed areas would be fumigated.

The effectiveness of glyphosate was called into question last year when Colombian anti-drug chiefs presented a report to their U.S. counterparts of the area of drug plantations they claimed to have destroyed.
U.S. satellite images later showed that plantations said to have been fumigated were still flourishing because rain had washed away the glyphosate herbicide.
According to government statistics, more than 150,000 acres (60,000 hectares) are given over to illicit drug plantations in the country.

The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration estimates that Colombia supplies 80 percent of the world's cocaine. Last month it issued a report saying Colombia had edged out Asia as the major supplier of heroin, of exceptionally high purity, to the United States.
